title: Sunny and the Autumn Leaves
description: Little Sonny the quokka discovers the magic of autumn for the first time. A cosy, gentle bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
One morning, Sunny woke up and noticed something different.

The big old gum tree at the edge of the clearing had changed overnight. Its leaves, usually green and still, had turned the most beautiful colours Sunny had ever seen.

Deep golden yellow. Warm burnt orange. A soft, gentle red, like the colour of the setting sun.

Sunny padded over slowly, his little nose twitching with curiosity.

One leaf let go of its branch — slowly, slowly — and drifted down through the cool morning air. Sunny watched it spin and twirl, this way and that, until it settled softly on the ground right in front of him.

He sniffed it gently. It smelled of earth and dry bark and something sweet he couldn't quite name.

Then another leaf fell. And another. Until the air was full of leaves drifting down like quiet little promises.

Sunny sat very still in the middle of it all, watching, breathing, feeling the soft cool air against his fur.

He didn't need to do anything. He didn't need to go anywhere. He just needed to be right here, in this gentle autumn morning.

After a while, he found the biggest, most beautiful leaf of all — golden and whole, with perfect little veins running through it like tiny rivers. He carried it carefully in his paws and brought it back to his favourite mossy rock.

He looked at it for a long, quiet moment.

Then he curled up beside it, tucked his chin to his chest, and let his eyes grow heavy.

The leaves kept falling all around him, soft and slow, like the whole world was getting ready to rest.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, leaves. Goodnight, beautiful autumn.
